content:
The image shows a corn leaf with a single, circular, light tan to white spot with a papery texture. It is roughly the size of a pencil eraser or slightly larger, has a light cream/tan center, no obvious dark border or ring, and appears on an otherwise healthy green leaf.

Key features:
- Circular, light tan/white spot, ~1/4 inch diameter
- Papery texture, cream/white center
- No dark pustules (rules out rust)
- No rectangular shape bounded by veins (rules out Gray Leaf Spot, Southern Corn Leaf Blight)
- No yellow halo visible here, but the spot is circular and isolated
- No cigar shape (rules out Northern Leaf Blight)
- No water-soaked margin or freckles (rules out Goss's Wilt)

This closely matches **Holcus Spot**: "Circular, oval, or irregular dark green water-soaked spots that dry to light tan or white with papery texture... Spots range from 1/8 to 1/4 inch in diameter and appear randomly across the leaf surface." The spot is circular, tan-to-white, papery, and randomly placed on the leaf — a classic Holcus Spot presentation.
